chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Barmaki. He said: al-Fadl ibn Sulayman al-Kufi narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Khalid. He said: I heard al-Rida Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them both) saying:

Allah, blessed and exalted, never ceased to be Knowing, Powerful, Living, Everlasting, Hearing, and Seeing. I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, there are people who say that He, mighty and majestic, never ceased to be Knowing with a knowledge, Powerful with a power, Living with a life, Everlasting with a lastingness, Hearing with a hearing, and Seeing with a sight. He (peace be upon him) said: Whoever says that and believes in it has indeed taken other gods besides Allah, and has no part in our wilaya at all.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: Allah, mighty and majestic, never ceased to be Knowing, Powerful, Living, Everlasting, Hearing, and Seeing by His Essence. He is far exalted above what the polytheists and the anthropomorphists say, greatly exalted.

key_terms.الْمُشَبِّهُونَ: Al-Mushabbihun (the anthropomorphists): those who liken God to creation by attributing separate qualities to Him
key_terms.لِذَاتِهِ: Li-dhatihi (by His Essence): the Shia theological principle that God's attributes are identical with His Essence, not superadded qualities
key_terms.وِلَايَتِنَا: Wilayatina (our wilaya/authority): allegiance to the Ahl al-Bayt and their theological teachings

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida teach about whether God's attributes are separate from His Essence?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) teaches that God's attributes of knowledge, power, life, eternity, hearing, and seeing are essential to His Essence (li-dhatihi) and not separate entities or hypostases. When al-Husayn ibn Khalid informs him that some people claim God is 'Knowing with a knowledge, Powerful with a power' and so forth — positing the attributes as distinct realities alongside God — the Imam strongly condemns this view, declaring that whoever holds it 'has taken other gods besides Allah' and has no part in the Ahl al-Bayt's wilaya. This represents a core Shia theological position against the Ash'ari doctrine of eternal attributes (sifat za'ida) and the Christian-influenced notion of divine hypostases.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us from Muhammad b. Isma`il al-Barmaki. He said: Al-Fadl b. Sulayman al-Kufi narrated to us from al-Husayn b. Khalid. He said: I heard al-Rida `Ali b. Musa (as) say:

Allah never ceased to be Knowing, Powerful, Living, Everlasting, Hearing, and Seeing. So, I said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah! There are a people who say: “He never ceased to be Knowing with knowledge, Powerful with power, Living with life, Everlasting with lastingness, Hearing with the ability to hear, and Seeing with sight.” So, he (as) said: Whoever says that and that which is close to that has taken other gods besides Allah; they are not upon our wilaya at all.
Then, he (as) said: Allah never ceased to be Knowing, Powerful, Living, Everlasting, Hearing, and Seeing by His Essence. He is far above what the pagans and those who liken Him to His creation say.
